# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (stated as budget holder)
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage. The Client has three stated AI use cases:

- a customer service chatbot deployed on the support portal
- an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line
- AI sales forecasting planned for next year

Three facts shape this proposal.

1. **Audit finding.** A June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems.
2. **Dated objective.** The stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
3. **Regulation and certification.** The EU AI Act and GDPR are the stated regulatory drivers. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year on a date that is not yet fixed.

Three constraints apply throughout:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement would hand Tamarack a finished set of documents. The Guided AI GRC Build works differently. The Client's own team builds the AI Management System (AIMS) week by week, with a live workshop, a coaching session and structured asynchronous work between sessions.

This matters for Tamarack for three reasons.

- **Familiar foundations.** The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The people who maintain those systems are the people best placed to extend them to AI.
- **Retained knowledge.** The knowledge needed to keep the AIMS running stays inside the Client, so the system does not depend on an outside party after Week 12.
- **Better starting point for ISO/IEC 42001.** A team that has built and operated the system is in a stronger position when that certification work starts. This is a readiness benefit, not a promise of certification.

The program uses two open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

The program operates under three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

### Inventory sequencing

The two systems that enter the Week 2 inventory first are the customer service chatbot and the visual inspection pilot.

- **Chatbot:** it is the only stated deployed system and it interacts with customers through the support portal.
- **Visual inspection pilot:** it carries the Sponsor's dated production objective for Q2 2027.

Sales forecasting enters the inventory as a planned system, so that it is governed from intake rather than after deployment. Any further AI systems in use at Tamarack are Unknown and will be discovered during Week 2.

### Spine

The readiness themes in the right-hand column describe preparation for ISO/IEC 42001. They do not indicate any certification outcome.

| Week | Spine focus | Tamarack tailoring | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scope covers the three stated use cases. Roles are assigned across the build team. Works council timing is logged as a delivery risk. | Context, scope and leadership |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot and visual inspection pilot are entered first, with sales forecasting as planned. This directly addresses the June 2026 internal audit finding. | Context and scope |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | Each inventoried system is classified against the EU AI Act and assessed for GDPR relevance. Confirm with external counsel. | Planning |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Impact assessments for the chatbot and the visual inspection pilot. Whether the chatbot processes customer data, and where, is Unknown and will be established here. | Operation and impact assessment |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | The register is populated from Week 4. Treatment owners are named by the Client. | Planning and risk treatment |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set, including data handling consistent with the EU data residency constraint. Confirm with external counsel. | Leadership and policy |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates are defined, including a pilot-to-production gate for visual inspection ahead of the Q2 2027 objective. | Operation |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Supplier review for the chatbot and inspection providers. Supplier identities are Unknown. Evidence collection begins. | Operation and third parties |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Two governed workflows are configured with defined human oversight points. Works council consultation is confirmed before anything touches production staff. | Operation and human oversight |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring is designed for chatbot outputs and inspection performance. Metrics are Unknown and will be set by the Client. | Performance evaluation |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change processes are defined. The first evidence review is held. | Improvement |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Evidence walkthrough against the six-element definition. | Performance evaluation and internal audit readiness |

### Integration with incumbent frameworks

The program attaches to existing structures rather than building parallel ones. The Profile Block names one artifact for integration: the June 2026 internal audit finding, which the Week 2 inventory addresses.

The specific ISMS and QMS artifacts that later weeks would attach to are Unknown. These include any risk register, policy set, supplier process, incident process, change process or audit programme. They will be identified at Week 1 and recorded as integration points once the Client confirms them.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS consisting of six elements:

1. an adopted charter
2. a populated inventory
3. an operating risk register
4. an adopted core policy set
5. at least two governed AI workflows in production use
6. evidence collection running for at least four weeks

Evidence collection starts at Week 8, which provides four weeks of running evidence before the Week 12 review.

**Scoping item for Week 1 steering.** The Profile Block states one deployed system, the customer service chatbot. The visual inspection system is in pilot, and whether it will be in production use before Week 12 is Unknown. The second governed workflow is therefore Unknown and must be identified and confirmed at Week 1 steering, drawing on the Week 2 inventory where needed.

## 5. Expected Client Team Commitment

The figures below are estimates per person per week. They cover the workshop, the coaching session and asynchronous work. Actual effort will depend on what the inventory finds and on the state of existing ISMS and QMS documentation.

| Role | Typical weekly hours (estimate) | Heavier weeks (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 2 to 3, plus about 2 in steering weeks | W1, W3, W6, W12 |
| CISO | 3 to 4 | W3, W8, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 3 to 5 | W4, W7, W10 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 | W2, W4, W10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 | W4, W7, W9 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 to 3 | W2, W11, W12 |

The combined estimate is about 18 to 27 hours per week across the team.

**Independence of internal audit.** The Client may wish to give the two internal auditors an advisory and assurance-design role rather than an ownership role. This would help protect their independence when they later audit the AIMS. The decision rests with the Client.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12. Steering attendees are Unknown and will be confirmed by the Client.

| Week | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Week 1 | Confirm scope, team, the second production workflow and works council timing. |
| Week 6 | Review spine status, blockers and any scope decisions. |
| Week 12 | Receive the evidence walkthrough and confirm the operating plan for the following year. |

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format**

- One live virtual workshop and one coaching session each week, with asynchronous work between sessions.
- The time zones for scheduling are Unknown and will be agreed at mobilization.

**Data handling**

- Repository assets are templates.
- Client records and evidence are held in Client-controlled storage, at a location to be confirmed by the Client, consistent with the EU data residency constraint.

**Price**

- The price is US$60,000, which falls within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Fiscal year dates and the invoicing schedule are Unknown and will be agreed at contract.

**Timing**

- The start date is Unknown.
- If Week 1 begins in the first week of January 2027, Week 12 falls in late March 2027, before Q2 2027.
- The decision to move visual inspection into production remains with the Client.

## 8. Items Requiring Confirmation

The following items carry legal effect. For each one, confirm with external counsel:

- EU AI Act classification of each system
- GDPR obligations for the chatbot and any other system processing personal data
- the EU data residency constraint as applied to AI suppliers
- the scope and timing of German works council consultation

Program outputs support readiness only. They are not a certification, audit or regulatory outcome.

## 9. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On a positive decision, the Client is asked to confirm four things:

1. a Week 1 start date
2. the named individuals for each build team role
3. the steering attendees
4. a provisional candidate for the second governed workflow in production use
